items.description: Where our GitHub App is installed: an account or organization.

account_type.description:
`user` or `organization` today. An open string: more values may come without a new
release, and a client keeps working on one it doesn't know.

repository_selection.description:
`all` (every repository of the account) or `selected` (only the ones chosen at install)
today. An open string: more values may come without a new release.

AuthConfig.description: An auth config, without its secret.

last_error.description: Why the last refresh or the consent failed.

refresh_task.description: The pending refresh task's name, and when it runs.

setup_complete.description:
Whether setup is complete: osiris holds the tokens and, when they can be refreshed, their
refresh is scheduled. When false, the connection can't be used.

status.description:
`pending` (the consent is open), `active`, `disabled` (no refresh is scheduled, so the
connection can't be used: after a failed connect the user must connect again; after a
refresh, osiris schedules it again by itself), `expired` (the provider refused a refresh
or the grant is gone: reconnect) or `failed` (the consent failed or was never finished). A
connection is only reported `active` when its setup is complete.

redirect_url.description: The provider's own consent page: send the browser here.

alias.description: Yours: a mark for this attempt, to find what it made if its answer is lost.

auth_config_id.description: `ac_…`: the provider's app to connect through.

callback_url.description:
Where the browser goes after the provider's consent, with `connected_account_id` and
`status` added to its query.

user_id.description: Yours: who the connection is for, such as an organization's id.

code.description:
`OS_00` unauthorized, `OS_01` not found, `OS_02` invalid request, `OS_03` conflict,
`OS_04` provider refused, `OS_05` provider unavailable, `OS_06` connection not active,
`OS_07` unknown version, `OS_08` idempotency key reused, `OS_09` request in flight,
`OS_99` internal.

EventDelivery.description:
An event as a subscriber receives it on the events topic, written in the API key's pinned
release. The type and the connection's id, never its data: fetch the connection for its state.

Fields may be added without a new release, so a subscriber ignores one it doesn't know.

event_id.description: `ev_…`, the same each time the event is delivered, so a client can drop repeats.

osiris_version.description: The API release the event is written in, also the message's `osiris_version` attribute.

type.description:
What happened, also the message's `type` attribute: `connection.active`,
`connection.expired` or `connection.revoked` today. An open string: new types may come
without a new release, and a client ignores a type it doesn't know.
